Out of the 19 disciples of Gurū Nānak mentioned by Bhāī Gurdās, two were Muslims-- Mardānā, a mīrasī or bard, from his own village, and Daulat Khān Lodi, an Afghān noble.

It was not a monastic order, but a fellowship of ordinary men engaged in ordinary occupation of life. A key element in this process of restructuring of religious and social life was the spirit of sevā.
